text:
alice: Heads up — ran into a weird TS / ESM issue when using the js-sdk in an edge runtime (Vercel Edge) where generics are getting erased and overload resolution fails.

ben: Ugh, details? SDK version?

alice: redwood-js-sdk@1.4.2 (local branch). Error shows \"No overload matches this call\" for our typed call with generic <T>. Works fine in node dev but fails after bundling for edge.

carmen: Do you have a repro? Is it tsconfig or the bundler (esbuild/webpack) changing module resolution?

alice: Minimal repro: in app:

```
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = createClient();

const resp = await client.generate<{name: string}>({ prompt: 'x' });
```

TS error: \"Generic type 'generate' requires 1 type argument(s)\" even though it's provided.

ben: That smells like TS can't find the .d.ts that has the generic overloads. Are we publishing types to both exports? Check package.json \"exports\" field.

dave: also saw failures where `unknown` in overloads becomes `any` after emit when using esbuild's ts transpileOnly flow. Bundlers can drop overload .d.ts resolution if paths differ.

alice: I checked — package.json has:

```
\"main\": \"dist/index.cjs.js\",
\"module\": \"dist/index.esm.js\",
\"types\": \"dist/index.d.ts\",
\"exports\": {
  \".\": {
    \"import\": \"dist/index.esm.js\",
    \"require\": \"dist/index.cjs.js\"
  }
}
```

but consumers on edge get the ESM file and the bundler resolves types to `index.d.ts` fine. Yet tsserver inside VScode (project using pnpm workspace) points to a different .d.ts under node_modules/.pnpm/..../node_modules which is missing overloads.

carmen: Could be hoisting + package manager flattening. Also tsconfig \"moduleResolution\": \"node\" vs \"bundler\" matters. For ESM packages TS sometimes prefers \"exports\" mapping only when moduleResolution is \"bundler\".

ben: Quick workaround: add a named export with an explicit type-safe wrapper so inference doesn't need overload resolution at callsite. But we should fix package types properly.

dave: Another library-level fix: publish per-entry-point d.ts files, and add \"types\" mapping inside \"exports\" like:

```
\"exports\": {
  \".\": {
    \"import\": { \"types\": \"dist/index.d.mts\", \"default\": \"dist/index.esm.js\" },
    \"require\": { \"types\": \"dist/index.d.cts\", \"default\": \"dist/index.cjs.js\" }
  }
}
```

Not all package managers respect it but TS 4.7+ does when moduleResolution=bundler.

alice: Any short term tsconfig advice for app teams? We can't force them to change bundler.

carmen: Recommend adding to tsconfig:

```
{\"compilerOptions\": { \"moduleResolution\": \"bundler\", \"skipLibCheck\": true }}
```

and to temporarily pin sdk to ESM-only import (import * as sdk from...)? Also turn on `preserveValueImports`? might not help.

ben: Also check `declarationMap` and ensure declarations are emitted for both .mts/.cts if you're using dual package.

build-bot: CI failure #1245: tsserver errors in examples/edge-sample on node 18 — see logs: https://ci.internal/1245

alice: Thanks — I'll open a small PR to (1) add exports->types mapping, (2) ensure our build emits .d.ts for both module formats, (3) add a note in README about tsconfig moduleResolution and edge bundlers.

dave: When you make the PR, let's also relax overloads to prefer generic parameter defaults instead of complex unions. Overloads with `unknown` vs `any` are biting consumers that suppress inference.

carmen: agree. For the long term we should add a tiny sample app that demonstrates correct tsconfig for edge use (esbuild + moduleResolution=bundler) and include it in the SDK examples.

alice: Filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/362 — description and checklist in the PR.

ben: Nice. I'll review. :thumbsup:

alice: if anyone hits the same, ping me and i'll share the repro link.
